outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no new first public argument on the conjecture as stated was found. The only general ZFC claim, Espíndola's arXiv 1906.09169 (current v7, 13 April 2022), predates the window and I found no journal record, referee report, or public verification of it. The 2024 Shelah–Vasey JEMS paper (first posted 16 May 2018) proves the conjecture only under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, or for AECs with amalgamation under a weak GCH.
problem_asks: (1) For every cardinal λ there exists a cardinal μ(λ): the threshold is a function of λ alone. (2) The quantification runs over all abstract elementary classes K with LS(K) ≤ λ, so one μ(λ) must work uniformly for every such K. (3) Hypothesis: K is categorical in some cardinal above μ(λ). (4) Conclusion: K is categorical in every cardinal above μ(λ). Parts (1)–(2) carry the uniformity in K; parts (3)–(4) are the transfer from one cardinal above the threshold to all cardinals above it. The statement assumes no amalgamation, no tameness, no large cardinal and no GCH-type hypothesis. Read from the statement alone, 'categorical in a cardinal above μ(λ)' is one cardinal, as the bullet says.

events.what_happened: Shelah, Classification Theory for Abstract Elementary Classes (College Publications, 2009), IV.7.12, claims the successor-cardinal hypothesis can be dropped, with upward transfer, for AECs with amalgamation under a weak GCH (2^μ < 2^μ+) and an unpublished claim 'to appear in [Shea]'. Shelah–Vasey (arXiv 1805.06291, §1.4) say the proof 'relied on a claim of [She09a, III.12] that was not proven there, but promised to appear in [Shea]'. Vasey (arXiv 1510.03780 abstract) says the successor hypothesis can be removed 'using an unpublished claim of Shelah' that the weak GCH holds. The book is a book, not a preprint; the schema has no book kind, so it is recorded as repository. I did not access the book itself; its content is taken from the two papers above.
events.revisions: Book 2009 (publisher listing in search results, not opened).
events.delivers: Categoricity at some λ above a threshold (the double-beth threshold beth_{beth_{(2^LS(K))+}} in Shelah's transfer, per Vasey's abstract) implies categoricity at all larger cardinals, for AECs with amalgamation, under weak GCH and the unpublished claim. Restricted to amalgamation plus weak GCH; the successor restriction is lifted only under those hypotheses. Per a search summary of Vasey's work (not verified in a text I read), the statement as printed is stronger than what the proof gives and is partly erroneous; I could not check this.
events.remains: The general AEC case in ZFC without amalgamation or GCH-type hypotheses, and the uniform-in-λ threshold form.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the expositions and follow-up papers that examine Shelah's argument; co-author of arXiv 1805.06291.
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote an exposition of the proof 'modulo the claim' (cited as [Vas17b, Section 11]) and flagged the claim as not proven in the place cited. Shelah–Vasey state in a footnote 'We prove this missing claim' (Corollary 14.4) and use it for the amalgamation result. I did not verify that proof.

events.doubts: The argument depends on an unpublished claim of Shelah, which the authors who examined it say was not proven where cited. Shelah–Vasey's footnote says they supply the missing claim in their own paper, so the gap may be closed, but I did not verify their Corollary 14.4. A search summary reports that the printed statement contradicts Morley's theorem; this is unverified in the text I read.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture under amalgamation plus weak GCH, conditional on the unpublished claim.

events.what_happened: Will Boney, 'Tameness from large cardinal axioms' (arXiv 1303.0550, v1 3 March 2013; later JSL 79(4), December 2014, DOI 10.1017/jsl.2014.30). Abstract: 'We show that Shelah's Eventual Categoricity Conjecture follows from the existence of class many strongly compact cardinals.' Method: every AEC with LS(K) below a strongly compact κ is <κ-tame, then the Grossberg–VanDieren categoricity transfer applies. Shelah–Vasey's introduction says the conjecture was known when the starting categoricity cardinal is a successor, citing Boney; the abstract I read has no such qualifier.
events.revisions: v1 3 Mar 2013; v2 18 Mar 2013; v3 15 Aug 2013; v4 13 May 2014. JSL 79(4) Dec 2014 (search result, not opened).
events.delivers: Under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, categoricity transfer for AECs by way of tameness. The abstract is unqualified; Shelah–Vasey read the result as covering only a successor starting cardinal. This scope conflict is unresolved.
events.remains: The large-cardinal hypothesis is not removed. The non-successor reading, if the abstract is taken at face value, is not settled. The uniform-in-λ threshold form is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed publication of the paper, JSL 2014.
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication (journal record from a search result, not opened).

events.direction: In favour of the conjecture, conditional on class many strongly compact cardinals.

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in universal classes: part I' (arXiv 1506.07024, v1 23 June 2015; v11 5 March 2017; Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 168(9), 2017, 1609–1642). Abstract (fetched): 'If K is categorical in cardinals of arbitrarily high cofinality, then K is categorical on a tail of cardinals.' The argument is in ZFC and needs no successor assumption. It generalises to AECs with a locality property and primes, and with amalgamation gives an explicit Hanf bound. The abstract says the proof 'stems from ideas of Adi Jarden and Will Boney, and also relies on a deep result of Shelah'.
events.delivers: For universal classes: categoricity in cardinals of arbitrarily high cofinality implies categoricity on a tail, in ZFC. This is a different hypothesis from the bullet's (categoricity in cardinals of arbitrarily high cofinality, not in one cardinal above a threshold). Second theorem, for AECs with amalgamation that are fully LS(K)-tame and short with primes over M ∪ {a}: categoricity in some λ above an H2 threshold implies categoricity in all λ' ≥ H2.
events.remains: Universal classes in the single-cardinal form (covered in Part II), and general AECs in the bullet's form. The AEC theorem needs tameness, shortness and primes.

checked_by.who: Annals of Pure and Applied Logic (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2017 (journal reference shown on the arXiv abstract page).

events.direction: In favour, restricted to universal classes (and to AECs with locality and prime-model hypotheses); the hypothesis is categoricity in arbitrarily high cofinality.

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'On prime models in totally categorical abstract elementary classes' (arXiv 1509.07024, v1 September 2015; later version v3 exists). Per a search snippet (not opened): for fully tame and short AECs with amalgamation, categoricity in all large cardinals is equivalent to having primes over sets M ∪ {a}; assuming a large cardinal axiom, the conjecture is equivalent to 'every AEC categorical in a proper class of cardinals eventually has prime models over M ∪ {a}'.
events.revisions: v1 September 2015 (from arXiv identifier; day not read); later versions to v3.
events.delivers: A conditional equivalence (a reduction), not a proof of the conjecture in the bullet's form, under a large cardinal axiom and full tameness/shortness.
events.remains: The conjecture itself: the reduction is to a different statement about prime models, and the large-cardinal hypothesis is not removed.
events.direction: Neutral-to-supporting: reduces the conjecture to a prime-model statement under a large cardinal axiom.

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in tame AECs with primes' (arXiv 1509.04102, v1 14 September 2015; Mathematical Logic Quarterly 64 (2018), 25–36). Abstract (fetched): 'A new case of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture is established.' Let K be an AEC with amalgamation, H2 the explicit beth-expression in LS(K), K H2-tame, and K_{≥H2} with primes over M ∪ {a}. If K is categorical in some λ > H2, it is categorical in all λ' ≥ H2. The paper also gives a homogeneous-diagram case.
events.delivers: A restricted case: AECs with amalgamation that are H2-tame and have primes over M ∪ {a} above H2. The threshold H2 is defined from LS(K) only, which is the uniform-in-λ form the bullet asks for. The categoricity hypothesis is a single cardinal above H2. Tameness and primes are extra hypotheses.
events.remains: AECs without H2-tameness or the prime-model hypothesis, which is most AECs in the bullet's statement.

checked_by.who: Mathematical Logic Quarterly (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (journal reference on the arXiv abstract page).

events.direction: In favour, restricted to H2-tame AECs with amalgamation and primes; the threshold is a function of LS(K).

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'Downward categoricity from a successor inside a good frame' (arXiv 1510.03780, v1 13 October 2015; earlier title 'A downward categoricity transfer for tame abstract elementary classes'; Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 168(3), 2017, 651–692). Abstract (fetched): downward transfer from categoricity in λ and θ+ to all of [λ, θ] for AECs with a type-full good frame. It improves the threshold in Shelah's transfer to beth_{(2^LS(K))+} under tameness, and 'the successor hypothesis can also be removed from Shelah's result by assuming in addition either that the AEC has primes over sets M ∪ {a}, or (using an unpublished claim of Shelah) that the weak generalized continuum hypothesis holds'.
events.delivers: Successor-hypothesis removal from Shelah's transfer under either primes or weak GCH plus the unpublished claim. The transfer uses categoricity at two cardinals (λ and θ+), not one. Restricted to AECs with a type-full good frame.
events.remains: The single-cardinal form of the bullet for general AECs, and any uniform-in-λ threshold. The weak-GCH branch rests on Shelah's unpublished claim.

checked_by.who: Annals of Pure and Applied Logic (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2017 (journal reference on the arXiv abstract page).

events.doubts: The weak-GCH branch depends on an unpublished claim of Shelah (stated in the abstract). I did not find that claim proven in any text I read.
events.direction: In favour under extra hypotheses (primes, or weak GCH plus an unpublished claim); two-cardinal transfer.

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in universal classes. Part II' (arXiv 1602.02633, v1 8 February 2016; Selecta Mathematica 23(2), 2017, 1469–1506, DOI 10.1007/s00029-016-0296-0). Abstract (fetched): 'We prove that a universal class categorical in a high-enough cardinal is categorical on a tail of cardinals.' It works in ZFC with no amalgamation, no large cardinals, and no successor assumption, with an explicit threshold. It also proves a conjecture of Grossberg for universal classes. The abstract does not describe the general AEC conjecture as open.
events.revisions: v1 8 Feb 2016; v2 6 Sep 2016; v3 26 Oct 2016. Selecta 2017.
events.delivers: Universal classes only, in the single-cardinal form of the bullet, in ZFC, with an explicit threshold. Per the abstract, the threshold is in terms of the vocabulary (search summary, Main Theorem 7.3; not verified in the text read).
events.remains: General AECs, which are not universal classes. The uniform-in-λ threshold for general AECs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2017 (journal reference on the arXiv abstract page).

events.direction: In favour, restricted to universal classes; single cardinal hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Sebastien Vasey, 'The categoricity spectrum of large abstract elementary classes' (arXiv 1805.04068, v1 10 May 2018; v7 2 October 2019). Abstract (fetched): classifies the possible categoricity spectra of AECs with amalgamation and arbitrarily large models under injective cardinal exponentiation (empty, an end segment below the Hanf number, or a closed interval of finite successors of LS(K)); under strengthened GCH, bounded or containing an end segment for classes without maximal models. Its only mention of the conjecture is 'This answers several longstanding questions around Shelah's categoricity conjecture'. The version list I read stops at v7 (2019); a search summary claimed a December 2024 version, which the fetched page does not support.
events.delivers: A classification of categoricity spectra (the set of cardinals with exactly one model), not an eventual categoricity transfer. It does not establish categoricity in all large cardinals from one.
events.remains: All of the bullet: the abstract does not address the eventual transfer.
events.direction: Neighbouring question (spectra, not eventual categoricity). Discarded for this bullet; recorded because the abstract names Shelah's categoricity conjecture.

events.what_happened: Saharon Shelah and Sebastien Vasey, 'Categoricity and multidimensional diagrams' (arXiv 1805.06291, v1 16 May 2018; v5 9 March 2023; Journal of the European Mathematical Society 26(7), 2024, 2301–2372; accepted 18 April 2024, published 15 May 2024). Abstract (fetched): using multidimensional diagrams in independent amalgamation, 'we show assuming the existence of a proper class of strongly compact cardinals that an AEC which has a single model of some high enough cardinality will have a single model in any high enough cardinal', and 'assuming a weak version of the generalized continuum hypothesis, we also establish the eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs with amalgamation'. Conjecture 1.3 (the AEC version) has no explicit Hanf number or LS(K) ≤ λ condition. Conjecture 1.2 (the L_{ω1,ω} version) is stated as still open.
events.delivers: Two conditional results. (i) Under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals: a single model at one high cardinal gives a single model at all high cardinals, which is categoricity transfer with a threshold that is 'high enough' and not explicit. (ii) Under weak GCH, for AECs with amalgamation. The threshold is not stated as a function of LS(K) alone in the parts I read.
events.remains: The general AEC conjecture in ZFC without large cardinals and without a GCH-type hypothesis. The uniform-in-λ threshold form. The L_{ω1,ω} version (Conjecture 1.2), which the paper says is still open.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed publication by the journal; authors are Saharon Shelah (Hebrew University, Rutgers) and Sebastien Vasey (Harvard).
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 18 April 2024 and published 15 May 2024 (EMS journal page). The arXiv acknowledgements thank 'the referees' and named experts (John Baldwin, Will Boney, Adi Jarden) for comments.

events.time_since_posted: 8 years 5 months (arXiv v1); 2 years 5 months since JEMS publication
events.doubts: Internal technical flags in the authors' own text (arXiv v5): footnote 3 says 'some technical points remain on how exactly to do this' in extending Corollary 14.7 from strongly compact to measurable cardinals; Remark 3.14(4) says 'we are stuck when λ is (probably weakly) inaccessible'; Fact 3.16(1) is flagged 'Pedantically this is not O.K.'. These are the authors' own flags, not an external verdict. No external verification was found.
events.direction: In favour, conditional on a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, or on weak GCH with amalgamation. The paper does not claim a ZFC proof.

events.what_happened: Christian Espíndola, 'A topos-theoretic proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes' (arXiv 1906.09169, v1 21 June 2019; title later changed). Abstract of v4 and v5 (fetched): 'Assuming GCH and that there is a measurable cardinal, we give a topos-theoretic proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes (AEC's).' v5 adds: the large-cardinal assumption 'can be spared assuming instead that the AEC satisfies the amalgamation property, which together with categoricity in a high enough cardinal is actually equivalent to eventual categoricity'. The same abstract says the work 'improves the state of knowledge about the open problems stated by Shelah, including one for L_{ω1,ω} sentences'. Talks were given on 30 April 2020 (Masaryk algebra seminar, abstract as a search snippet) and 7 May and 22 October 2020; the write-up date is the arXiv date.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jun 2019 (topos-theoretic, GCH + measurable); v2 3 Jul 2019; v3 25 Jul 2019; v4 7 Aug 2019 (GCH + measurable, as read); v5 28 Aug 2019 (adds the amalgamation route, as read); v6 28 Dec 2020 (retitled 'An extension of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture to accessible categories with directed colimits'); v7 13 Apr 2022 (see the next event). v2 and v3 not read.
events.delivers: Under GCH and a measurable cardinal, eventual categoricity for AECs in the form 'categorical in two cardinals implies categorical in all in between' with the Hanf-number threshold. With amalgamation, the author claims the large-cardinal hypothesis is unnecessary, but the abstract does not say whether GCH is still needed on that route.
events.remains: The conjecture in ZFC without GCH and without a measurable cardinal, and any uniform-in-λ threshold. The version with the amalgamation route is not settled by the abstract.
events.doubts: Conditional on GCH and a measurable cardinal. The later version (v7) claims to drop both, which means the v1-to-v5 argument was replaced rather than extended; see the 2022 event for the doubts about that replacement.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture, conditional on GCH plus a measurable cardinal.

events.what_happened: Christian Espíndola, 'A short proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AEC's with no maximal models, under GCH' (arXiv 1909.13713, v1 30 September 2019). Abstract (fetched): 'We provide a short proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AEC's with no maximal models, assuming the Generalized Continuum Hypothesis (GCH).' It also proves a downward categoricity transfer for axiomatizable AECs with no maximal models. By v3 (28 December 2020) the title is 'with interpolation, under GCH', per the fetch summary; the v3 comments say interpolation is necessary and sufficient over ZFC 'because GCH can be removed by forcing arguments'. That comment is the author's, not verified.
events.revisions: v1 30 Sep 2019 ('no maximal models', GCH); v2 2 Oct 2019; v3 28 Dec 2020 ('with interpolation', GCH; comments say GCH can be removed by forcing).
events.delivers: Under GCH: eventual categoricity for AECs with no maximal models (v1) or with interpolation (v3). Restricted classes and a GCH hypothesis.
events.remains: The conjecture in ZFC for general AECs. The v3 claim that GCH can be removed by forcing is not shown in the text I read.
events.doubts: The v3 comment says GCH can be removed by forcing; I did not verify that step. The v1 and v3 hypotheses differ (no maximal models vs interpolation), with no change note.
events.direction: In favour, under GCH and for restricted AEC classes.

events.what_happened: Espíndola's arXiv 1906.09169 v6 (28 December 2020, the same day as v3 of 1909.13713) retitled 'An extension of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture to accessible categories with directed colimits'. Per the fetch summary of the abstract (not a quoted text), for AECs with interpolation the author obtains 'a proof, in ZFC, of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture'; the general accessible-category results assume GCH and a proper class of strongly compact cardinals. This is the earliest version I can confirm carries a ZFC claim. v2 to v5 were not read for this.
events.revisions: v6 28 Dec 2020 (as described above; summarised from fetch, not quoted).
events.delivers: A ZFC proof of the conjecture for AECs with interpolation (per the abstract summary), with a necessary and sufficient interpolation condition. Restricted to AECs with interpolation.
events.remains: General AECs without interpolation. Also the accessible-category extension, which needs GCH and strongly compact cardinals in this version.
events.doubts: The same date's v3 of 1909.13713 says the interpolation result is under GCH, which seems to conflict with a ZFC claim for interpolation AECs at v6 of 1906.09169. The conflict is between two papers by the same author, both dated 28 Dec 2020; I could not resolve it from the summaries I had.
events.direction: In favour, restricted to AECs with interpolation, if the v6 summary is right.

events.what_happened: Christian Espíndola, 'A proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture and an extension to accessible categories with directed colimits' (arXiv 1906.09169, v7, 13 April 2022; the current version). Abstract (fetched from the arXiv HTML): 'We provide a proof, in ZFC, of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes (AEC's).' No amalgamation or interpolation hypothesis is attached to the AEC claim. Assuming in addition the Singular Cardinal Hypothesis, the author extends the result to accessible categories with directed colimits. The Comments field says 'Arguments are now cast in ZFC for abstract elementary classes'. The introduction calls the conjecture 'the main open problem in the area' and says 'the full conjecture has been open until now'. Main AEC result: Corollary 9.6 (per fetch summary), 'Let K be an AEC. Then there exists a cardinal μ0 such that if K is categorical in some λ>μ0, it is categorical in all λ'>μ0', with μ0 'the maximum of the Hanf numbers for categoricity and non-categoricity' and 'the threshold cardinal we find is not explicit'. The corollary is said to follow from Theorem 9.3, which assumes SCH (fetch summary). Section 10 says 'in many of the results on AEC's, GCH can be removed', but its opening was not visible in the fetch.
events.revisions: v7 13 Apr 2022 (current; title changed from v6). No change note beyond the Comments field.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: eventual categoricity for all AECs in ZFC, in the bullet's shape (categorical in some cardinal above a threshold implies categorical in all cardinals above it). The threshold is per K (max of Hanf numbers), not shown to depend only on LS(K). Whether the AEC corollary depends on SCH or GCH through Theorem 9.3 and Section 10 is unresolved from the text I could read.
events.remains: Whether the threshold can be taken as a function of λ alone, uniformly over all K with LS(K) ≤ λ, as the bullet requires. Whether every step of the claimed ZFC removal is complete (Section 10 not fully read).

checked_by.who: Anonymous commenter on the nLab forum (unnamed; undated in the search snippet)
checked_by.qualification: Unknown. The remark says the commenter has 'some informal information'.
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote that the work is 'very interesting to model theory community but it is not yet independently checked nor widely accepted', and that 'some parts of the argument are not clear to the experts' (per search snippet). The page returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so this is a snippet, not read in full. The remark may predate v6 or v7.

events.doubts: (a) No journal record, referee report, erratum or expert verification found in four years; Espíndola's own homepage lists the preprint with no status or date (fetched). (b) Scope grew between versions: the ZFC claim at v6 (Dec 2020) is for AECs with interpolation, and at v7 (Apr 2022) for all AECs, with no change note beyond 'Arguments are now cast in ZFC'. (c) The AEC corollary reportedly follows from Theorem 9.3, which assumes SCH (fetch summary); the GCH and SCH removal is said to be in Section 10, not fully visible to me. (d) The threshold is not explicit and is not shown to depend only on LS(K). (e) The paper's own claim that a forcing argument 'adapts well in this particular proof' and that some lemmas are 'not difficult to see' (Lemma 2.6) or 'readily generalizable' (§3.5) are brief justifications, per the fetch summary. (f) The anonymous nLab remark above, seen only as a snippet.
events.direction: In favour: a claimed proof of the conjecture for AECs in ZFC. Not published; not verified in any record I found.

events.what_happened: Mazari-Armida and Wentao Yang, 'Building models in small cardinals in local abstract elementary classes' (arXiv 2310.14474; first submitted October 2023, revised April 2024). Per a search snippet (not opened): builds models in small cardinals without categoricity assumptions, addressing Grossberg's question for small cardinals; 'one key step relies on an unproven claim of Shelah that they could not verify'.
events.revisions: First submitted October 2023; revised April 2024 (search snippet).
events.delivers: Model-building in small cardinals for local AECs, not a categoricity transfer. Does not bear on the conjecture's threshold.
events.doubts: The authors, per the snippet, rely on an unproven claim of Shelah in a key step. Recorded as a pattern: this is the same kind of unpublished claim as in the 2009 event, but it is not about the conjecture's threshold.
events.direction: Neighbouring question (model-building in small cardinals). Discarded for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah ([BLS24], as cited in Baldwin's Logic Seminar abstract of 25 February 2025). Per that abstract (not the paper, which I did not open): an L_{ω1,ω} sentence categorical in ℵ0 and ℵ1 with a model in ℶ1+ is ω-stable. The abstract also says that whether there is a similar example for L_{ω1,ω} remains open.
events.revisions: Not established; the paper was not opened and its month is unknown.
events.delivers: Countable L_{ω1,ω} sentences categorical at ℵ0 and ℵ1 are ω-stable. Concerns the sibling L_{ω1,ω} categoricity question at small cardinals, not an AEC threshold μ(λ) for all K with LS(K) ≤ λ.
events.remains: The bullet's statement for general AECs, and the uniform threshold.
events.direction: Neighbouring question (sibling L_{ω1,ω} categoricity). Discarded for this bullet, though it is near the L_{ω1,ω} case that Shelah–Vasey list as Conjecture 1.2.

events.what_happened: Georgios Marangelis, 'Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities' (arXiv 2410.19515, single version, 25 October 2024). Abstract (fetched): generalises ℵ1-Kurepa-tree results to ℵ_{α+1}-Kurepa trees, builds an L_{ω1,ω}-sentence ψ_α, and shows consistency results for the spectrum and for local Hanf numbers below 2^{ℵ0}. The 'Shelah's conjecture' in question concerns the local Hanf number below 2^{ℵ0} for L_{ω1,ω} sentences (model existence), not categoricity or eventual categoricity.
events.delivers: Consistency results on local Hanf numbers and amalgamation spectra for L_{ω1,ω} sentences at higher cardinals. No categoricity or eventual categoricity result.
events.remains: All of the bullet. The paper is about a different Shelah conjecture that shares a name.
events.direction: Different question sharing a name ('Shelah's conjecture'). Discarded for this bullet; recorded because it is the only in-window arXiv paper on a Shelah conjecture that a search turns up.

summary: I ran 40 searches and read or fetched about 25 sources; the in-window picture is that nothing new was posted on this conjecture in the window, and the settled cases are restricted. The central item is Espíndola's arXiv 1906.09169. It was first posted on 21 June 2019 as a topos-theoretic proof under GCH plus a measurable cardinal (v1–v5, abstract read for v4 and v5). It was retitled and revised in v6 (28 Dec 2020) and v7 (13 April 2022). The current v7 abstract claims a ZFC proof of the conjecture for all AECs, with SCH assumed only for the accessible-category extension. I found no journal record, referee report or erratum, and Espíndola's own page lists the preprint with no status. The scope widened between versions without a change note: the v6 ZFC claim is, per the fetch summary, for AECs with interpolation, and v7 extends it to all AECs. The v7 AEC corollary (Corollary 9.6) is said by the fetch summary to follow from Theorem 9.3, which assumes SCH, while the GCH removal is in Section 10, whose opening was not visible. The threshold is 'the maximum of the Hanf numbers for categoricity and non-categoricity' and 'not explicit'; I did not find it stated as depending only on LS(K), which the bullet's μ(λ) requires, and the Section 10 text is the place to check. The second main source is Shelah and Vasey (arXiv 1805.06291, first posted 16 May 2018; JEMS 2024). They prove the conjecture under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, and for AECs with amalgamation under weak GCH. Their Conjecture 1.3 has no LS(K) condition. The text I read does not mention Espíndola's 2019–2022 claims, and their §1.4 says the earlier amalgamation proof depended on an unpublished claim of Shelah, which they say they prove in Corollary 14.4. Earlier partial results are Boney (strongly compact, successor case per Shelah–Vasey, arXiv 2013, JSL 2014); Vasey's universal-class results (Part I 2015 with a cofinality hypothesis, Part II 2016 with a single cardinal and explicit threshold, Selecta 2017); Vasey's tame-with-primes case (2015, MLQ 2018, threshold a function of LS(K)); and Vasey's downward transfer (2015, APAL 2017), which uses Shelah's unpublished claim for the weak-GCH branch. Shelah's 2009 book claims the successor hypothesis can be dropped under amalgamation and weak GCH, relying on that same claim. For the date rule, the only in-window dated items are the JEMS publication of the 2018 paper (May 2024), which is not an in-window first argument, and two neighbouring papers (Marangelis, October 2024, on a local Hanf number; BLS24, 2024, on countable L_{ω1,ω}). The AI search found nothing: no source names an AI system in connection with this conjecture. Searches for lab announcements, AI trackers, Lean formalisations and AI-acknowledgements returned only unrelated items, such as OpenAI's May 2026 Erdős unit-distance result and DeepMind's Aletheia on Erdős problems, neither concerning categoricity. The reviewed claims are the JEMS, APAL, MLQ, Selecta and JSL records; the Espíndola ZFC claim has only an anonymous undated nLab remark. Close calls: (a) whether Espíndola's v7 claim is a resolution, as its abstract says, or a conditional claim with unresolved dependencies (SCH via Theorem 9.3, GCH via Section 10, and a threshold not shown to be a function of λ); (b) whether the Shelah–Vasey 2024 paper, at the bullet's scope, is a restricted case, since it needs large cardinals; (c) whether the Shelah 2009 claim and Vasey's downward result should count, given they rest on an unpublished claim that Shelah–Vasey say they prove.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading this as resolved: Espíndola's v7 (13 April 2022) states the bullet's conjecture for all AECs in ZFC, in a form whose hypotheses ('categorical in some cardinal above a threshold implies categorical in all above it') match the bullet. The paper is 4.5 years old and was revised across several versions, which is normal for a long argument, and nobody has refuted it in the sources I found. Its method is categorical logic with κ-classifying toposes, as the abstracts say, and the author has published related work (with Kanalas, TAC 2025). Under that reading the claim stands unrefuted and is the first public written argument for the general case. Against that: no review, no publication, a scope change between v6 and v7 with no change note, an SCH-dependent corollary, an unseen GCH-removal section, and a threshold that is not stated as a function of λ alone, which the bullet requires. The landmark-with-no-uptake signal is the strongest point against counting it.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A journal record, referee report or erratum for arXiv 1906.09169 v7 (none found). (b) An expert statement, from Vasey, Boney, Shelah, Grossberg or Baldwin, on whether Section 10's GCH-removal and Corollary 9.6's SCH dependence hold, and whether the threshold can be made a function of LS(K) alone. (c) The full text of v6 and v7, to see exactly what changed in scope and whether the AEC claim now carries SCH or GCH. (d) Whether the JEMS version of Shelah–Vasey (2024) cites or addresses 1906.09169; the arXiv v5 text I read does not mention it. (e) A formal verification (none known). (f) The Section 10 argument, and the textual status of Shelah's unpublished claim: whether Shelah–Vasey's Corollary 14.4 really proves it.
